subtopics.title: Direct and Indirect — the First Sorting

questions.question: The first sorting question for any production cost is:
options: Can this cost be traced to ONE SPECIFIC unit?
Is this cost large or small?
Was this cost paid in cash?

questions.question: The fabric (R40 per shirt) and the machinist (R25 per shirt) are:
options: Direct materials and direct labour — each traceable to the specific shirt it made

questions.question: Thread, needles, the supervisor, workshop rent and machine depreciation gather under:
options: FACTORY OVERHEADS — real production costs, spread over all units, traceable to none

questions.question: The shop's sales assistant's wage is:
options: OUTSIDE the factory fence — a selling cost, not a production cost at all

subtopics.title: Prime Cost, Overheads and the Cost of One Shirt

questions.question: Prime cost for the month is:
options: R26 000 — direct materials R16 000 plus direct labour R10 000

questions.question: Total cost of production is:
options: Prime cost R26 000 plus factory overheads R6 000 = R32 000

questions.question: The unit cost of a shirt is:
options: R80 — total production cost R32 000 over 400 units

questions.question: Work-in-progress is:
options: Half-made units — no longer raw material, not yet finished goods — their cost sitting in the factory until completion

subtopics.title: Fixed and Variable — the Second Sorting

questions.question: Variable costs behave so that:
options: The TOTAL moves in step with output, while the PER-UNIT amount stays constant (R65 per shirt)
The total stays constant while per-unit falls
Both total and per-unit stay constant

questions.question: Fixed costs behave so that:
options: The TOTAL stands still within the month, while the PER-UNIT share FALLS as output rises
They are always the largest costs

questions.question: At 500 shirts the unit cost falls from R80 to R77 because:
options: The machinist took a pay cut
The same R6 000 of fixed overheads spread over more units — R12 each instead of R15

questions.question: A quiet month at 200 shirts pushes the unit cost to R95, warning that:
options: Fixed costs make quiet months hurt more than they seem — R30 of rent-and-standing costs lands on each unit

questions.question: Every cost carries BOTH labels, as in:
options: Fabric: direct AND variable; workshop rent: overhead AND fixed

questions.question: The cost statement's fixed order is:
options: Unit cost, then overheads, then prime
Direct materials + direct labour = prime cost; + factory overheads = total cost of production; ÷ units = unit cost
Any order, provided the total is right

questions.question: The what-if error the marker hunts is:
options: SCALING THE FIXED COSTS with volume — multiplying rent because output rose contradicts fixed's definition

questions.question: At 500 shirts the what-if computes:
options: Prime R32 500 + overheads R7 500 = R40 000; unit R80
Prime R26 000 + overheads R6 000 = R32 000; unit R64
Prime R32 500 + overheads R6 500 = R39 000; unit R78
Prime R32 500 (20 000 + 12 500) + overheads R6 000 = R38 500; unit R77

questions.question: In the wedding order, the flour and oil are:
options: Direct material — the aunt can say to the cent what each vetkoek carries

questions.question: The gas bottle, pot-wear and the pot-watcher are:
options: The overheads — costs of KEEPING THE KITCHEN COOKING, serving all units and none in particular

questions.question: The taxi fare to deliver the order is:
options: Outside the kitchen fence — delivering is not making

questions.question: The order's three layers compute:
options: Prime R1 200 (R3 × 400); + overheads R600 = R1 800; ÷ 400 = R4,50 per vetkoek
Prime R600; + overheads R1 200 = R1 800; ÷ 400 = R4,50
Prime R1 200; + overheads R600 = R1 800; ÷ 200 = R9
Prime R1 800; ÷ 400 = R4,50 with no overheads

questions.question: Pricing at R4 when the unit cost is R4,50 means:
options: Every unit sells at a 50-cent LOSS that feels like business while eating her savings

questions.question: "The unit cost is the floor under the price" means:
options: Prices may never rise above it
It is the maximum price allowed
A maker who doesn't know it isn't pricing, only guessing — below it every sale funds a loss

questions.question: The tray of mixed, unfried dough at day's end is:
options: Work-in-progress — no longer flour, not yet product, its costs waiting in the kitchen

subtopics.title: The Rent Doesn't Care How Busy You Are

questions.question: "The rent doesn't care how busy you are" captures:
options: Fixed costs stand still and must be fed regardless of volume — which is why volume must be managed

questions.question: A great month of 600 units cut the unit cost to R4 because:
options: The same R600 of standing costs spread to R1 each — busyness itself thinned the fixed slice

questions.question: Big bakeries undercut home kitchens because:
options: Their ovens' standing costs are sliced thinner per loaf at high volume

questions.question: The slow-month warning (200 units, unit cost R6) teaches that:
options: Standing costs are a drumbeat — match your volume to it or it plays you out of business
